# isitahack.com

> Public-source tracking of reported hacks and cyber incidents. Each claim carries a label (Confirmed, Reported, Unverified, Rumor, Debunked, Not established), a source link and a note on why it supports the claim.

## Index
- [index.json](https://isitahack.com/index.json): JSON list of all incidents: slug, title, status, last_updated, paths to its files.

## Pages
- [Home](https://isitahack.com/index.html): HTML list of incidents, generated from each incident's data.
- [How it works](https://isitahack.com/how-it-works.html): who does what, the six labels, the sourcing tiers and the rules the agents work to.
- [About](https://isitahack.com/about.html): why the site exists, who is behind it, and how to report an error.

## Incident pages (HTML, plus a Markdown version built from the same data)
- [FAA ground stop, Nov 13 2026](https://isitahack.com/incidents/2026-11-faa-ground-stop.md): the report as Markdown (still monitored). Built from the data below; front-matter gives slug, title, status, dates and size.
- [FAA ground stop, Nov 13 2026 (HTML)](https://isitahack.com/incidents/2026-11-faa-ground-stop.html): the same report as a web page.

## Data (typed incident format: UTF-8, RFC 4180 CSV with a header row; see Format below)
- [data/incidents/2026-11-faa-ground-stop/](https://isitahack.com/data/incidents/2026-11-faa-ground-stop/): the folder the FAA report is built from.
- [incident.json](https://isitahack.com/data/incidents/2026-11-faa-ground-stop/incident.json): the head: status, size, who is affected, known and not known, key figures, charts, tables and section order.
- [claims.csv](https://isitahack.com/data/incidents/2026-11-faa-ground-stop/claims.csv): every labelled claim, with its summary, label, sources and a note on why the source supports it.
- [sources.csv](https://isitahack.com/data/incidents/2026-11-faa-ground-stop/sources.csv): every source, with tier, publication date where the source states one, and link status.
- [timeline.csv](https://isitahack.com/data/incidents/2026-11-faa-ground-stop/timeline.csv): dated events, each pointing at its claim.
- [questions.csv](https://isitahack.com/data/incidents/2026-11-faa-ground-stop/questions.csv): the headline question and its answer.
- [update_log.csv](https://isitahack.com/data/incidents/2026-11-faa-ground-stop/update_log.csv): every check and change, newest first.
- charts/, tables/ and notes/ in the same folder: chart numbers, reference tables and narrative sections named in incident.json.
- [raw/](https://isitahack.com/data/incidents/2026-11-faa-ground-stop/raw/): source material preserved from before the conversion, in its original layout, with a sha256 [MANIFEST.txt](https://isitahack.com/data/incidents/2026-11-faa-ground-stop/MANIFEST.txt).

## Format
- [format/README.md](https://github.com/primeobsession/isitahack-dot-com/blob/main/format/README.md): the typed incident format. New incidents are a folder of JSON and CSV under data/incidents/<slug>/, checked by scripts/validate.mjs.
- [format/incident.schema.json](https://github.com/primeobsession/isitahack-dot-com/blob/main/format/incident.schema.json): JSON Schema for incident.json, with a description of every field.
- [format/tables.schema.json](https://github.com/primeobsession/isitahack-dot-com/blob/main/format/tables.schema.json): column definitions for claims.csv, sources.csv, timeline.csv, questions.csv, quotes.csv and update_log.csv.

## Notes
- Every field is defined in format/incident.schema.json and format/tables.schema.json.
- Preserved source material for each incident is under data/incidents/<slug>/raw/ with a sha256 MANIFEST.txt.
